1.q: הַ⁠דָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל בָּבֶ֖ל
1.note: Jeremiah is using **The word that Yahweh spoke concerning Babylon** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Here, **hand** represents “agency.” The phrase **by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet** means that Yahweh gave this message through Jeremiah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [through Jeremiah the prophet]

2.note: A **banner** is a kind of flag on a pole that people raised as a signal, here to call armies together or to announce important news. If your readers would not be familiar with what a banner is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and lift up a signal flag on a pole]

2.q: אִמְרוּ֩ נִלְכְּדָ֨ה בָבֶ֜ל הֹבִ֥ישׁ בֵּל֙ חַ֣ת מְרֹדָ֔ךְ הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ עֲצַבֶּ֔י⁠הָ חַ֖תּוּ גִּלּוּלֶֽי⁠הָ
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Say that Babylon has been captured, that Bel has come to shame, that Marduk is dismayed, that her idols have come to shame, and that her images are dismayed]

The expression **Babylon has been captured** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who did the action, the context indicates that it is the enemy nation that attacks Babylon. This also occurs in verse 24. Alternate translation: [An enemy nation has captured Babylon]
The words **Bel** and **Marduk** are the names of false gods that the people of Babylon worshiped. Bel was a title for Marduk, the chief god of Babylon.

Yahweh is speaking of **Her idols** and **her images** as if they were living things that could feel shame and dismay. He means that the idols of Babylon will be shown to be worthless and powerless. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Her idols have been shown to be worthless; her images have been proven powerless]

3.note: The pronoun **It** refers to the nation that will come against Babylon from the north. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [That nation, it will set]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **dweller**. He means dwellers in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and there will not be any people dwelling in her]

Yahweh is referring to all of the living creatures in Babylon by naming two major components, **man** and **beast**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Every living creature]

4.note: Yahweh is using the phrase translated as **In those days and in that time** to introduce a new event in this prophecy. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. This also occurs in verse 20.
See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8. This also occurs in verses 10, 20, 21, 30, 35, and 40.

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **go** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [They will keep on walking and weeping]
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:13. This also occurs in verse 28.

5.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [They will tell one another to come, and they will join themselves to Yahweh]

The word translated as **‘Come!’** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This command appears abruptly in Hebrew without an introductory phrase like “they will say.” Scholars have proposed that with different vowels on the original consonants, it would say “They will come,” which continues the description in the rest of the verse. Both the ULT and UST follow the standard Hebrew text (with the UST expressing the command dynamically as “They will urge one another”). You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [They will come.]

Yahweh is using **their faces are facing this way** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they are determined to go this way,” that is, toward **Zion**. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they will be determined to go in this direction]

The expression **will not be forgotten** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who will do the action, it is the people who make this covenant with Yahweh. Alternate translation: [they will not forget]

6.note: Yahweh is speaking as if his people were **a lost flock** of sheep that had wandered away from its pasture. He means that they have turned away from him and are in danger. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My people have turned away from me and are in danger]

Yahweh is speaking as if the leaders of Israel were **shepherds** who had led their sheep astray. He means that the leaders caused the people to stop obeying him and to worship false gods. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their leaders have led them to worship false gods]

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were sheep that wandered **from mountain to hill** looking for pasture. He means that they went from one place of idol worship to another, since people often worshiped idols on mountains and hills. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They went from one place of idol worship to another]

7.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the enemies of his people were wild animals that had **devoured** them. He means that their enemies attacked and destroyed them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All of their finders have attacked and destroyed them]

7.q: וְ⁠צָרֵי⁠הֶ֥ם אָמְר֖וּ לֹ֣א נֶאְשָׁ֑ם תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָטְא֤וּ לַֽ⁠יהוָה֙ נְוֵה צֶ֔דֶק וּ⁠מִקְוֵ֥ה אֲבֽוֹתֵי⁠הֶ֖ם יְהוָֽה
7.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and their adversaries have said that they were not guilty, because the people had sinned against Yahweh, the pasture of righteousness and the hope of their fathers, Yahweh]

The adversaries are speaking as if Yahweh were **the pasture of righteousness**, a place where sheep can safely find food. They mean that Yahweh was the one who righteously provided for and protected his people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [against Yahweh, the one who righteously provided for and protected them]

The adversaries are using this possessive form to describe a **pasture** that is characterized by **righteousness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the righteous pasture]
The adversaries are using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their ancestors]

8.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **male goats** go out first **before the face of the flock**, so Yahweh’s people should be the first to leave Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and be the first ones to leave]

9.q: הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֡י מֵעִיר֩ וּ⁠מַעֲלֶ֨ה עַל בָּבֶ֜ל
9.note: Yahweh is using **behold** with the words **I am stirring up and bringing up** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am about to stir up and bring up.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to stir up and bring up against Babylon]

Yahweh is speaking of causing nations to attack Babylon as if he were stirring up something, such as water. He means that he is causing these nations to take action against Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [am rousing] or [am motivating]

The expression **she will be captured** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who will do the action, it is the **assembly of great nations**. Alternate translation: [from there they will capture her]

The point of this comparison is that just as a skilled **warrior** succeeds in battle, so the **arrows** of the enemy soldiers will hit their targets. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [His arrows will hit their targets as surely as a skilled warrior succeeds in battle]

Yahweh is using **does not return empty-handed** as a common expression of the culture to mean “always succeeds in what he tries to do.” Since this is connected to the comparison of the arrows to a wise warrior, this means the arrows will hit their targets. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly as in the UST. Alternate translation: [he always succeeds in what he tries to do]

11.q: כִּ֤י תשמחי כִּ֣י תעלזי שֹׁסֵ֖י נַחֲלָתִ֑⁠י
11.note: The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing the Babylonians, the **plunderers of my inheritance**, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is speaking as if his people were his **inheritance**, property that belonged to him permanently. He means that the Babylonians have plundered the people and land of Israel, who belong to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [plunderers of the people and land that belong to me]

11.q: כִּ֤י תפושי כְּ⁠עֶגְלָ֣ה דָשָׁ֔ה ו⁠תצהלי כָּ⁠אֲבִּרִֽים
11.note: The point of these comparisons is that just as **a heifer threshing** jumps about and **mighty ones**, that is, strong horses, neigh loudly, so the Babylonians celebrated wildly when they plundered Yahweh’s people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [though you celebrate wildly, jumping about and shouting loudly the way a young cow threshing grain jumps about and strong horses neigh]

12.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the city of Babylon were the **mother** of the Babylonians, **the one bearing you**. He means that the city and nation of Babylon will be greatly ashamed and humiliated. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Your city, Babylon, is greatly ashamed; the land where you were born is humiliated]

Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Indeed, the last of nations]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to mean that Babylon will be the **last**, that is, the least important, of all the **nations**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the least important nation]

The terms **wilderness**, **dry land**, and **desert** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [is a totally uninhabitable place]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wrath**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Because Yahweh is so angry]

13.q: וְ⁠הָיְתָ֥ה שְׁמָמָ֖ה כֻּלָּ֑⁠הּ כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עַל־בָּבֶ֔ל יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְ⁠יִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־כָּל־מַכּוֹתֶֽי⁠הָ
13.note: See how you translated similar phrases in 19:8.

Hissing was a symbolic action by which people showed that they were shocked at something and scorned it. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and will hiss in shock and scorn over all of her wounds]

14.q: עִרְכ֨וּ עַל בָּבֶ֤ל סָבִיב֙ כָּל דֹּ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת יְד֣וּ אֵלֶ֔י⁠הָ אַֽל תַּחְמְל֖וּ אֶל חֵ֑ץ כִּ֥י לַֽ⁠יהוָ֖ה חָטָֽאָה
14.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Since Babylon has sinned against Yahweh, array yourselves against her all around, all of the ones bending a bow! Shoot at her; may you not spare an arrow]

Jeremiah is using one part of an action, **bending a bow**, to mean all of the actions of archers and therefore archers themselves. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all you archers]

Yahweh is speaking of **arrows** as if they were something a person could show mercy to by sparing them. This means that the soldiers should shoot all their arrows at Babylon without holding any back. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shoot all your arrows]

15.note: Yahweh is using **She has given her hand** as a common expression of the culture to mean “she has surrendered.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [She has surrendered]

The word **buttresses** refers to a kind of strong structure, such as a tower, that supported and protected the walls of a city. If your readers would not be familiar with what buttresses are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [her supporting towers have fallen]

The expression **have been torn down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who did the action, it is the enemies who attack Babylon. Alternate translation: [her attackers have torn down her walls]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vengeance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [For it is Yahweh who is avenging himself]

16.q: כִּרְת֤וּ זוֹרֵ֨עַ֙ מִ⁠בָּבֶ֔ל וְ⁠תֹפֵ֥שׂ מַגָּ֖ל בְּ⁠עֵ֣ת קָצִ֑יר
16.note: Yahweh is referring to all of the people who work on farms in Babylon by naming two major components, **the sower** and **the one grasping the sickle at the time of harvest**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Cut off all the farmers from Babylon]

Here, **the oppressing sword** represents “the cruel enemy army” that kills people with swords. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [From the face of the cruel enemy army]

Yahweh is using **From the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of” or “on account of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Because of]

17.note: Yahweh is speaking as if Israel were **a scattered sheep**. He means that the Israelites have been forced to leave their land and live in many different places. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Israel has been forced to leave its land and live in many different places]

Yahweh is speaking as if the kings who attacked Israel were **lions** that had chased away a sheep. He means that powerful enemy kings forced the Israelites out of their land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [powerful enemy kings have forced him out of his land]

17.q: הָ⁠רִאשׁ֤וֹן אֲכָל⁠וֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְ⁠זֶ֤ה הָ⁠אַחֲרוֹן֙
17.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **first**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. **The first one** refers to the first of the two kings who attacked Israel, and **this last one** refers to the second king. Alternate translation: [Earlier, the king of Assyria devoured him, and now]

Yahweh is speaking as if Nebuchadnezzar were a lion that **has broken** the **bones** of Israel. He means that Nebuchadnezzar has completely defeated the Israelites. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [has completely defeated him]

18.q: לָ⁠כֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
18.note: Jeremiah is using **thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

**Behold me** is an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to visit punishment]
See how you translated the similar expression in 18:13.

19.q: וְ⁠שֹׁבַבְתִּ֤י אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל נָוֵ֔⁠הוּ וְ⁠רָעָ֥ה
19.note: In this verse, the word **Israel** is singular in form, but it refers to all the Israelites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a plural form such as “the Israelites” along with plural pronouns. Alternate translation: [And I will bring the Israelites back to their pasture, and each one of them will graze on]

Yahweh is speaking as if Israel were a flock of sheep that he will bring back to **his pasture**. He means that he will bring the Israelites back to their own land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will bring Israel back to his own land]

Yahweh is using **soul** to represent the whole person, here meaning the Israelites themselves. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will be satisfied]
See how you translated the similar expression in 31:6.

20.note: The expression **will be sought** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who will do the action, you could use a general expression such as “people” or “anyone.” Alternate translation: [people will search for the iniquity of Israel]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the wicked things that Israel did]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the sins of Judah will be sought, and they will not be found]
See how you translated the similar expression in [17:1](ta:17). Alternate translation: [the wicked things that Judah did]

21.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the command **go up** before the information about **the land of Merathaim**. Alternate translation: [Go up against the land of Merathaim]

21.q: הָ⁠אָ֤רֶץ מְרָתַ֨יִם֙ עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֶל יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י פְּק֑וֹד
21.note: The words **Merathaim** and **Pekod** are the names of regions in Babylonia. The name Merathaim sounds like a word in the original language that means “double rebellion,” and the name Pekod sounds like a word that means “punishment.”

To **devote** people **to destruction** was to destroy them completely as an act of dedication to God. If your readers would not be familiar with this practice, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [Destroy them; completely destroy them as an offering to me]

The pronoun **you** refers to the army that Yahweh is sending to attack Babylon. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and you, army attacking Babylon, do according to all that I have commanded you]

22.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 4:6.

23.q: אֵ֤יךְ נִגְדַּע֙ וַ⁠יִּשָּׁבֵ֔ר פַּטִּ֖ישׁ כָּל הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ
23.note: Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of astonishment. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Look at how the hammer of all the earth has been cut down and broken]

Yahweh is speaking as if Babylon were **the hammer of all the earth**, a tool used to smash other nations. He means that Babylon had crushed and destroyed many nations. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the nation that crushed all the other nations]

The expression **has been cut down and broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who did the action, it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [has fallen and shattered to pieces]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **a horror**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a horrifying thing]

24.note: Here, **Babylon** represents the people of Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I laid a snare for you and you were also captured, people of Babylon]

Yahweh is speaking as if he were a hunter who **laid a snare** to catch Babylon like an animal. He means that he caused Babylon to be captured suddenly when it did not expect it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I planned a surprise attack against you]

The expression **You were found and also seized** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who did the action, it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [I found you and also seized you]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [for you have contended against me]

25.q: פָּתַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת א֣וֹצָר֔⁠וֹ וַ⁠יּוֹצֵ֖א אֶת כְּלֵ֣י זַעְמ֑⁠וֹ
25.note: Jeremiah is speaking as if the armies that attack Babylon were **weapons** that Yahweh kept in **his storehouse** and **has brought out**. He means that Yahweh is sending these armies to punish Babylon. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has sent out the armies that he will use to punish Babylon in his anger]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **indignation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the weapons that he uses when he is very angry]

26.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. He means “Come to her from the distant parts of the earth.” You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Come to her from the far ends of the earth]

The point of this comparison is that just as farmers pile grain into **heaps** at harvest time, so the attackers should pile up everything in Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [pile up everything in her as farmers pile grain into heaps at harvest]
See how you translated this phrase in verse 21. Alternate translation: [and destroy her completely for Yahweh]

27.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the soldiers of Babylon were **bulls** that are taken to **the slaughter**. He means that the young warriors of Babylon will be killed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Destroy all of her young warriors; they will be killed]

Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of alarm about the disaster that is coming on the Babylonians. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How dreadful it will be for them]

The implication is that Babylon’s **day** refers to the time when Yahweh will punish Babylon. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for the time for them to be punished has come]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **visitation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the time when Yahweh will punish them]

28.q: ק֥וֹל נָסִ֛ים וּ⁠פְלֵטִ֖ים מֵ⁠אֶ֣רֶץ בָּבֶ֑ל לְ⁠הַגִּ֣יד בְּ⁠צִיּ֗וֹן
28.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [There is a sound of fugitives and of survivors from the land of Babylon declaring in Zion]

Jeremiah is using the possessive form to mean the vengeance that Yahweh takes on the Babylonians because they destroyed **his temple**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his vengeance for the destruction of his temple]

29.note: See how you translated these same phrases in verse 14. Alternate translation: [All you archers]
The words **her** and **she** refer to Babylon.

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **escape**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [Trap everyone inside of her]

30.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **men** that are characterized by **war**, that is, the soldiers who fight for Babylon. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and all of her fighting men]

The expression **will be silenced** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who will do the action, it is the enemy soldiers who attack Babylon. Alternate translation: [and all of the men of her war will become silent] or [and enemy soldiers will silence all of the men of her war]

Yahweh is referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase **will be silenced**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [will be killed in that day]

31.note: Here, **presumption** represents “Babylon, which is so presumptuous.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [presumptuous Babylon]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:13.
See how you translated this phrase in verse 27.

Yahweh is speaking of punishing Babylon as if it were something that he would **visit** upon them. It means that he will come and punish them for their sins. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the time when I come and punish you]

32.note: Even though Yahweh has been addressing Babylon directly, he is now speaking of it in the third person as **presumption**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [And you, presumptuous one, will stumble and fall]

Yahweh is speaking as if Babylon were a person who will **stumble and fall**. He means that Babylon will be defeated. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And presumption will be completely defeated]

32.q: וְ⁠הִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּ⁠עָרָ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠אָכְלָ֖ה כָּל סְבִיבֹתָֽי⁠ו
32.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the **fire** were an animal that will **devour** everything around it. He means that the fire will completely burn up everything around the cities of Babylon. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it will completely burn all of those around him]

The pronoun **his** refers to Babylon, which Yahweh has called **presumption**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And I will kindle a fire in the cities of Babylon]

33.note: The expression **are oppressed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who did the action, it is **their captors**. Alternate translation: [Their captors oppress the sons of Israel]

34.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **contend** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [He will surely plead their case]

35.note: Here, **sword** represents “war,” in which people are killed with swords. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [War will come against the Chaldeans]

36.note: The implication is that **the liars** are people in Babylon who spoke falsely. This may refer to (1) the diviners and false prophets of Babylon who claimed to know the future. Alternate translation: [A sword is against the diviners of Babylon who speak lies or (2) boastful men who made empty claims. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [A sword is against the boastful men who made empty claims]

37.note: The pronoun **his** refers to Babylon, spoken of here as a man, or possibly to the king of Babylon. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [A sword is against Babylon’s horses and against its chariots]

The implication is that **the mixed company that is in her midst** refers to foreign soldiers whom Babylon had hired to fight for it, along with other foreigners who lived there. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [all of the foreign soldiers and other foreigners who are in her midst]

The point of this comparison is that just as **women** are weaker and thus more afraid of physical violence than men, so the soldiers of Babylon will become weak and afraid. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and they will become weak and afraid]

The expression **they will be plundered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who will do the action, it is the enemies who attack Babylon. Alternate translation: [A sword is against her storehouses, and her enemies will plunder them]

38.note: In the original language, the word translated **drought** sounds very similar to the word translated “sword” in the previous verses. This is poetic language. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here.

Jeremiah is using the possessive form **land of carved images** to describe a land that is characterized by carved images. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a land filled with carved images]

Here, **terrors** represents “terrifying idols.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and by their frightening idols they act madly]

39.note: The terms **desert beasts** and **hyenas** refer to kinds of wild animals that live in deserted places. The exact identity of these animals is uncertain. If your readers would not be familiar with these animals, you could use the names of similar animals that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [wild desert creatures will dwell with wild dogs]

The pronouns **her** and **she** refer to Babylon. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in Babylon. And Babylon will not be inhabited … and Babylon will not be dwelt in]

Yahweh is using **unto generation and generation** as a common expression of the culture to mean “forever.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at any time in the future]
See how you translated the similar expression in 17:6. Alternate translation: [And people will not live in her]

40.q: כְּ⁠מַהְפֵּכַ֨ת אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת סְדֹ֧ם וְ⁠אֶת עֲמֹרָ֛ה וְ⁠אֶת שְׁכֵנֶ֖י⁠הָ
40.note: The point of this comparison is that just as God completely destroyed **Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighbors**, so he will completely destroy Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [God will completely destroy Babylon just as he completely overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns around them]

40.q: כְּ⁠מַהְפֵּכַ֨ת אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת סְדֹ֧ם וְ⁠אֶת עֲמֹרָ֛ה
40.note: Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **God**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [As when I overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah]

40.q: לֹֽא יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְ⁠לֹֽא יָג֥וּר בָּ֖⁠הּ בֶּן אָדָֽם
40.note: Here the masculine terms **man** and **son of man** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [no person will dwell there, and a human will not sojourn in her]

41.note: Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Pay attention, a people is coming from the north]

The expression **are being stirred up** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who does the action, it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [are coming because Yahweh is stirring them up from the remote parts of the earth]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:22.

42.note: In this verse, the words **bow** and **curved sword** are singular in form, but they refer to the bows and swords of all the soldiers as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural forms “bows” and “curved swords.” Alternate translation: [They grasp bows and curved swords]

42.q: קֶ֣שֶׁת וְ⁠כִידֹ֞ן יַחֲזִ֗יקוּ אַכְזָרִ֥י הֵ֨מָּה֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ קוֹלָ⁠ם֙ כַּ⁠יָּ֣ם יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְ⁠עַל־סוּסִ֖ים יִרְכָּ֑בוּ עָר֗וּךְ כְּ⁠אִישׁ֙ לַ⁠מִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָלַ֖יִ⁠ךְ בַּת־בָּבֶֽל
42.note: See how you translated a very similar verse in 6:23.

43.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **report** about the approaching army, not a report that the army made. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [The king of Babylon has heard the report about them]

Yahweh is using **his hands have become feeble** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he has lost his strength and courage.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he has become helpless with fear]
See how you translated this expression in 6:24. Alternate translation: [Distress seizes him as anguish seizes a woman giving birth]

44.note: Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Pay attention to this: like a lion he will come up from the pride of the Jordan]

44.q: כְּ⁠אַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִ⁠גְּא֣וֹן הַ⁠יַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒
44.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a lion** comes out of the thick bushes to attack sheep in a pasture, so the enemy will suddenly come to attack Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [the enemy will attack Babylon as suddenly as a lion comes up from the thick bushes of the Jordan to a pasture beside a stream that always has water]
See how you translated this expression in 12:5.

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **a pasture** that is characterized by **a permanent stream**, that is, a pasture beside a stream that always has water. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a pasture beside a stream that always has water]

The pronoun **them** refers to the flock, meaning the Babylonians who are pictured as sheep in the pasture, whom Yahweh will make run away from their city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [so in a moment I will make the Babylonians run from her]

Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis, to show that he alone chooses whomever he wants to rule over Babylon. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And I will appoint over her whomever I choose.]

44.q: כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֨וֹ⁠נִי֙ וּ⁠מִ֣י יוֹעִדֶ֔⁠נִּי וּ⁠מִֽי זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְ⁠פָנָֽ⁠י
44.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that no one is like him and that no one can challenge him or resist him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For no one is like me, and no one will summon me! And there is no shepherd who will stand before my face!]

44.q: וּ⁠מִֽי זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְ⁠פָנָֽ⁠י
44.note: Yahweh is speaking as if a ruler were a **shepherd**, and he is using **stand before my face** to mean resisting him. He means that no ruler can oppose him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And who is this ruler who will oppose me]

45.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **counsel**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh has decided that he will do]

45.q: אִם־לֹ֤א יִסְחָבוּ⁠ם֙ צְעִירֵ֣י הַ⁠צֹּ֔אן אִם־לֹ֥א יַשִּׁ֛ים עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֖ם נָוֶֽה
45.note: Following the custom of the culture, Jeremiah is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). Using this form and verbs in the present tense shows how certain it is that this will happen. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [If they do not drag them away, the little ones of the flock, then may I be cursed! And I solemnly swear that he will make their pasture desolate over them!]

Jeremiah is speaking as if the people of Babylon were **the little ones of the flock**, young sheep that enemies drag away. He means that the enemy will take away even the weakest Babylonians. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [even the weakest of the Babylonians]

46.note: Jeremiah says **the earth has quaked** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means that people everywhere will be shocked when Babylon is captured. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [people all over the earth have been greatly shocked]

The expression **has been heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must say who did the action, you could say that people everywhere heard it. Alternate translation: [and people everywhere have heard an outcry among the nations] or [and people in nations everywhere have been crying out]
